full_judgment:
10. I have been taken through the judgments pronounced by the Courts below as well as the evidence on record. Certain facts are admitted in this case. Opposite party No. 1 Toyezuddin is admittedly a co-sharer of the disputed holding. The sale deed sought to be pre-empted was registered under Section60 of the Registration Act on 21.8.78 and the application for pre-emption was filed on 18.12.78. Thus it is evident that application under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was filed within time. 

 14. In this connection, the learned Advocate for the opposite party has relied on the decision referred above. But this decision does not appear to be precisely on the point but the principle laid down may be availed of in coming to correct decision. In the cited case the transfer was saddled with agreement for reconveyane on condition that if the consideration money, he paid back by purchaser to the seller within certain time, then purchaser would recover the land and that seller having repaid the consideration money within the stipulated time, the purcharser reconvened the land to the seller. Subsequently seller transferred the land for the second time to a stranger but the co-sharer of the holding to which land appertained, instead of having pre-empted the second transfer, filed an application under Section 261, the then Bengal Tenancy Act, seeking pre-emption of the 1st transfer. Their Lordships of the Calcutta High Court held that the 1st sale was an absolute sale and that the condition of reconvey of the property cannot operate to excluded the application of Section 26F. In the instant case the heba deed though executed on 2.7.77 was registered on 11.4.79 and the disputed sale deed sought to be pre-empted was registered on 21.8.78 under Section 60 of the Registration Act i.e. prior to the registration of the deed of Heba-bil-ewaz. So. the deed of Heba-bil-ewaz cannot have the effect of destroying the right of pre-emption nor can affect right of pre-emption inasmuch as a party at his own will cannot suspend the operation of statute. 

 15. In view of this legal position the transfer of the disputed land as per registered deed of Heba-bil-ewaz cannot exclude the operation of Section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
